<!--
NUMBER PENDING, as for the other rebuilt supplements; the set is numbered once it is known. The
supplements written against the superseded figure are parked in
`../in_progress/figure_4_supplements_20260731/`.

WHAT IT IS. Figure 4, unchanged in every respect except the roster: the same two moments on the
same shared factor scale, the same rows pinned to the union, the same two line families, the same
nesting moment > member > parameter. What changes is which members hold the columns. Here they
are the four rungs INSIDE the recursive family, in the order figure_3.Rmd walks them:

    R    Recursive           recursion alone, one instant per interval
    MR   Mean Recursive      conditions on the interval MEAN, one interval end
    VR   Variance Recursive  removes the between-endpoint variance, still one end
    IR   Interval Recursive  conditions on BOTH ends, and restores it in the gain

R and IR are in the body figure and are carried here on purpose: without them MR and VR would be
two columns with nothing to be measured against, and with them the reader sees the whole step R
to IR and where the two intermediate rungs actually fall inside it.

16 columns rather than the body's 18 (no LSE, which fits with the unitary current held fixed and
so has no N_ch column, and four full members instead of four and a half). Fewer columns means a
LARGER cell and a TALLER figure, since the isotropy ties them: 0.181 in per decade against the
body's 0.157, 1.31 mm of cell against 1.14, and 7.40 x 6.63 in of page against 7.40 x 5.85.

WHAT IT SHOWS. Measured at noise 0.1, medians over the seven intervals:

                        N_ch:      10       100      1000     10000
    distortion, k_off   R        1.425    1.487    1.481    1.456
                        MR       1.448    1.778    1.777    1.942
                        VR       1.361    1.484    1.516    1.589
                        IR       1.367    1.127    1.025    1.006
    distortion, N_ch    R        0.844    1.130    1.267    1.297
                        MR       1.027    1.534    1.678    1.712
                        VR       0.957    1.361    1.480    1.516
                        IR       0.826    0.912    0.960    0.983
    bias in N_ch        R      +0.1335  +0.1513  +0.1396  +0.1387
                        MR     +0.1748  +0.1570  +0.1850  +0.1949
                        VR     +0.0564  +0.0699  +0.1200  +0.1259
                        IR     +0.0080  -0.0023  -0.0010  +0.0003

THE RUNGS DO NOT INTERPOLATE, and that is the whole point of the figure. Going from R to IR is an
improvement of a factor 1.45 in the k_off distortion; the two rungs in between are not at 1.3 and
1.15, they are ABOVE R. MR is worse than R in every column of every block here: 1.94 against 1.46
at N_ch 1e4, 1.71 against 1.30 in the channel number, and a bias of +0.195 against +0.139. VR
recovers part of it and stays above R in the second moment (1.59) while being the best of the
three in the first (+0.126). So conditioning on ONE interval end and stopping there costs
something, and adding the variance correction without restoring it in the update recovers the
mean and not the covariance. The distance from R to IR lives in the GAIN, not in the variance
model, and this is the plane-wide version of that claim.

CAUTION, two of them.

  The ordering depends on the measure. `figure_3.Rmd` reports MR 1.63 against R 1.17 on the
  ellipse-area measure at its own cell and puts VR worse still; here, on the per-parameter
  distortion medianed over the intervals at noise 0.1, VR sits BELOW MR. Both are true of what
  they measure. Whatever ends up in a caption has to name the measure and the cell, not just the
  ordering.

  MR's and VR's failure is not a coding error. It is the closure: MR carries the TOTAL conductance
  variance per start state, where IR carries the residual variance conditioned on both ends, so
  the between-endpoint spread that IR resolves through the boundary cross-covariance in the gain
  is instead dumped into the observation noise. A centred MR that fixed the calibration would be
  IR.

COVERAGE, and it is ragged on purpose. R and IR carry the full staircase, to noise 1e7 at N_ch
1e4; MR has three levels (0.1, 1, 10) and VR two (0.1, 1) at each channel count. Because the rows
are pinned to the union, those two members show as short bands with grey above, which is what
"not swept" should look like and is the reason this figure is not quietly like-for-like. About 40
per cent of the panel area is grey as it stands. VR falls under `MIN_CONTOUR_LEVELS` and is drawn
as tiles rather than as a two-row contour, which would be a linear ramp wearing the clothes of a
field. Both revert on their own as the runs land, with no edit here.

The alternative, which is NOT what this file does: pin the rows to the common grid instead of the
union, i.e. show all four members over the two decades where all four were measured. That gives a
7.40 x 3.15 in figure with no grey at all and a genuinely like-for-like comparison, at the price
of hiding how much less of the plane MR and VR cover. It is one line (YLIM) if the coverage stops
being a moving target.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
# The recursive family, cheapest rung first. No LSE and no NR/INR: this figure is about what
# happens INSIDE the recursion, and the open-loop members answer a different question, which is
# the body figure's.
FIG4_ALGOS     <- c("macro_R", "macro_MR", "macro_VR", "macro_IR")
FIG4_ALGO_LAB  <- c(macro_R = "R", macro_MR = "MR", macro_VR = "VR", macro_IR = "IR")
# a202e03 is listed although no least-squares arm is drawn here: the shared source CSVs are
# stamped by the COUNT of input files (figure_4_data.R:245), so a notebook that cannot see that
# directory rebuilds them without the un-averaged arm and every other figure then loses a column.
FIG4_DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/87889e6", "../data/0ffbda7", "../data/1f7138b",
                    "../data/a202e03")
source("figure_4_common.R")
source("figure_4_layout.R")
```

```{r sides}
# The same two sides as the body figure, read the same way, so a column here can be laid against
# a column there without a conversion: bias at theta_sim from battery_sim_G, distortion at
# theta_pool from battery_pool_G, both as a log10 factor on the shared scale.
SIDES <- list(
  list(lab = "distortion-induced bias", letter = "A",
       data = bias,                                  zf = function(x) x$Bconf),
  list(lab = "information distortion",  letter = "B",
       data = dplyr::filter(stat, comp == "total"),  zf = function(x) log10(x$Dconf)))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.4, fig.height = 6.63}
# 16 columns, so per_row is NOT the body's. MEASURED, not solved: a synthetic render of this same
# layout at 16 columns puts 0.204 at x 0.1817, y 0.1807, 99.5 per cent isotropic
# (tmp/calib_fig4.R, tmp/measure_fig4.py). The cell comes out 1.32 mm, wider than the body's 1.14.
fig4_render(SIDES, per_row = 0.204, out = "Figure_4_S2.pdf")
```

```{r measured-table}
# THE TABLE THIS FILE'S HEADER CARRIED BY HAND, generated instead, for the same reason as in
# figure_4_S1.Rmd: a note that repeats a measurement is a note that will one
# day disagree with it. The manuscript quotes these numbers, so they have to come from the render.
# READ FROM `m`, NOT FROM `Dconf`. Dconf is the CI edge toward the null (figure_4_data.R:199) and
# collapses to exactly 1 wherever the bootstrap interval brackets it, which is what the MAPS want
# and the wrong quantity for a table of values.
NOISE_LAB <- 0.1                  # the LABEL. S_tilde = label/10 = 0.01 (noise_units.R)
rl <- stat %>%
  dplyr::filter(comp == "total", param %in% PARAM_LONG,
                as.numeric(noise) == NOISE_LAB, is.finite(m)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(param, algo, Num_ch) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(m), nint = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(algo = factor(unname(ALGO_LAB[algo]), levels = unname(ALGO_LAB))) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(param, algo)

cat("\n=== information distortion, medians over the swept intervals, noise label ", NOISE_LAB,
    " (S_tilde = ", NOISE_LAB / 10, "), from m ===\n", sep = "")
rl %>% dplyr::select(param, algo, Num_ch, med) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Num_ch, values_from = med, names_prefix = "N_ch_") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)

# THE ORDERING CLAIM, stated as the comparison the manuscript makes: is MR worse than R, and does
# the gap grow with the channel count? Printed so the sentence in 04_results.tex has a source.
cat("\nMR against R, and VR against R, on each parameter (ratio of the two medians):\n")
rl %>% dplyr::select(param, algo, Num_ch, med) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = algo, values_from = med) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(MR_over_R = MR / R, VR_over_R = VR / R, IR_over_R = IR / R) %>%
  dplyr::select(param, Num_ch, MR_over_R, VR_over_R, IR_over_R) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```
